title: No-fault liability claims - the faster compensation route explained
p1:
What if you could claim compensation after an accident without first proving who was at fault?

Many people don't know that the law provides a quicker route in certain accident cases.
p2: A common belief is that every compensation claim requires a long battle to prove someone's mistake. But no-fault liability works differently. It focuses on providing faster financial relief instead of waiting for a lengthy fault investigation.
p3:
In simple terms, eligible victims can receive compensation without proving negligence by another person. The idea is to support victims quickly, especially when immediate medical expenses and financial pressures arise.

The key takeaway: faster compensation does not always mean the final question of responsibility disappears. It simply creates a quicker support mechanism while legal issues may continue separately.
conclusion: Did you know accident compensation could sometimes be claimed without proving who caused the accident? Would this faster route make the legal process more accessible?
